Quick technical summary from the on-call triage (09:03):
- Observed: sudden surge in connection attempts and retries from Maple Health's client IP block beginning 08:38 PT. Queue depth on the fronting proxies climbed, which pushed requests into backend timeouts and caused cascading 429 (rate limiter) and 5xx (upstream timeouts).
- Preliminary root cause hypothesis: client side backoff misconfiguration combined with a short-lived spike in request fanout. Their retry logic drove a retry storm once some requests hit transient timeouts.

Immediate mitigation applied (09:06):
1) Temporarily tightened per-customer token rate limit to 60 RPS from 200 RPS for Maple Health to reduce overload.
2) Enabled model-fallback routing for their route -> routes to a CPU-backed variant with higher concurrency but slightly higher latency (will reduce backend pressure).
3) Increased autoscaler aggressiveness for the affected pool (scaleUp target +2 nodes) as a safety margin.
4) Began rebalancing existing long-running KV-cache sessions to free up capacity.

Observed effect (09:09): 5xx spike reduced from ~35% to ~12%, latency p95 trending down but tail still elevated. Continuing to monitor.

Next steps:
- Ask Maple to pause aggressive retries for 15 minutes if possible (graceful backoff).
- Prepare a short status page update and coordinate on messaging.
- Will capture relevant logs and attach to the action plan: MAPLE-MUTUAL-ACTION-PLAN.xlsx and error_dump_20260302.log (attached).

I'll keep this thread updated every 15 minutes or sooner if anything changes.
